prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Miami for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” is subjective and depends on your needs (complexity, budget, insurance, location). I can narrow it down if you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood, whether you prefer a specialist (oral surgeon, periodontist, prosthodontist) or a general dentist who places implants, and if you have insurance.

Meanwhile, here’s a quick guide to find the best implant dentist in Miami and what to look for:

What type of clinician to consider
- For straightforward implants: experienced implant dentist or periodontist.  
- For complex cases (bone grafting, sinus lifts, multiple extractions): oral and maxillofacial surgeons or periodontists.  
- For the final restoration (crowns/bridges on implants): a prosthodontist or a general dentist with strong prosthetic experience.

Credentials and experience to prefer
- DDS or DMD plus documented implant training (postgraduate residency, fellowship, or continuing education).  
- Memberships/board certification: American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID), American Academy of Periodontology, American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, American College of Prosthodontists.  
- Years of implant experience and an implant case portfolio (before/after photos).  
- Regular use of 3D imaging (CBCT) and digital planning/guided-surgery techniques.

Questions to ask a dentist before committing
- How many implants do you place per year and what is your success rate?  
- What implant systems do you use (Straumann, Nobel, Zimmer, etc.)?  
- Will you do the entire procedure (placement + restoration) or coordinate with a specialist?  
- Do you do CBCT scans and guided implant planning?  
- What are all costs (implant, abutment, crown, bone grafts, CT scans, follow-ups)?  
- What is the timeline from placement to final crown?  
- Do you provide a warranty or guarantee and what follow-up care is included?

Where to search and compare providers
- Google/Google Maps (look at number of reviews and read recent ones)  
- Healthgrades, Zocdoc, RealSelf, Yelp  
- AAID “Find an Implant Dentist” directory and local dental society listings  
- Ask for referrals from your general dentist

Typical cost & timeline (rough estimates)
- Single implant (surgery + abutment + crown): often $3,000–$6,000+ depending on materials and additional procedures.  
- Bone grafting/sinus lift adds cost and time (several months healing).  
- Implant process can take 3–9+ months depending on healing and grafts.

Red flags
- No before/after photos or case history.  
- Pressure to accept a quick “same-day” implant without proper imaging or planning.  
- Extremely low prices with no explanation of implant brand/quality.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood in Miami and whether you prefer a specialist or need someone who takes your insurance, and I’ll pull a short list of highly rated implant dentists/clinics with contact info and what patients say about them.
